Hi Priya —

Thanks for taking this early conversation. We're evaluating Redwood to power a light-weight claims summarization workflow that will touch PHI in a subset of records. Procurement asked I start by clarifying a few requirements so we can size the procurement and privacy review:

- Residency: must keep all production PHI in us-east-1 only (no cross-region backups).
- Retention windows: default retention for claims transcripts is 7 years for legal/regulatory, but we also need a shorter operational retention (30/90/365 days) for cached models.
- Deletion: when we request deletion we need a verified audit trail (who/when) and an option for immediate hard delete vs deferred purge.
- Redaction: we need recommended patterns for redacting directly-identifying fields (SSNs, policy numbers) prior to sending to hosted inference, and whether tokenization or field-level hashing is preferable.

I've attached a sample data export (haven_data_schema.csv) that shows the fields expected. Can you outline Redwood's supported options and any constraints we'd need to include in procurement language (SLA/contract addendum)?

Appreciate a short written Q&A we can share with Legal/Procurement. If useful, happy to do a 30-min tech call next week.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Retention + deletion options for regulated claims data

Laura —

Thanks for the clear summary and the sample schema — that's helpful. Below is a short Q&A draft that covers the options we typically propose for regulated workloads; I flagged a couple follow-ups below. Happy to convert to a formal addendum once we lock the approach.

1) Residency
- Hosted: We can pin customer data and inference to a single region (us-east-1) for both runtime and persistent stores. Backups are configurable and can be limited to the same region; we do not replicate to EU/APAC by default for pinned accounts.

2) Retention windows (recommended patterns)
- Operational cache: configurable TTLs at the model endpoint level. Typical presets we recommend: 30/90/365 days. Cache is stored encrypted and scoped to your account.
- Persistent logs/artifacts: default retention is 7 years for audit/legal if you choose to retain; we can alternatively configure 1/3/7 year buckets.
- Ephemeral mode: if you prefer minimal retention, we offer an "ephemeral" config that deletes inference payloads after tokenization and never writes the raw text to persistent logs (recommended for high-sensitivity data).

3) Deletion semantics
- Soft delete: marks records for deletion and makes them inaccessible via API; data removed from search/indexing but retained in immutable backups until purge window.
- Hard delete: cryptographic shredding of data on primary storage; note that hard delete of backups follows the backup provider's retention and overwrite schedule unless you're on Dedicated/Private where we can guarantee immediate scrub in the customer's environment.
- Auditability: every delete request is logged with requestor identity, timestamp, and deletion mode. We provide an exportable audit log and an immutable deletion receipt for legal proof.

4) Redaction approaches and tradeoffs
- Client-side redaction (recommended when feasible): remove or tokenise SSNs/policy numbers before sending. Pros: highest control, no PHI leaves your environment. Cons: you need consistent token mapping if model outputs should preserve referential integrity.
- Ingest-time redaction (server-side preprocessor): field-level hashing or format-preserving tokenization at the API gateway. Pros: lower integration burden. Cons: intermediate PHI touches our ingest layer (we recommend VPC/Private for regulated workloads).
- Model-aware redaction: combine a small tokenizer map for identifiers and train the prompt to replace tokens; useful when you need templates in outputs.

Follow-ups we need from you:
- Do you require hard-delete of backups on demand, or are 30/90/180-day backup overwrite windows acceptable?
- Is referential integrity (the ability to map a token back to an original ID under controlled conditions) required for downstream workflows?

Attachments: I attached a brief PDF that summarizes these options and a sample mutual action plan template. If this looks good we can: (1) set up a 30-min technical call with Marissa (Solutions) to cover redaction patterns; and (2) have Legal draft a short addendum for procurement.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales (Regulated Industries)
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. Draft language suggestions below (short-form, to be polished by Legal Ops):

1) Residency and backups (suggested MSA clause)"Customer Data shall be stored and processed exclusively within the AWS us-east-1 region unless otherwise agreed in writing. Redwood will not replicate Customer Data to regions outside of us-east-1 for backup or disaster recovery unless explicitly authorized by Customer."

2) Deletion receipts and auditability"Upon request, Redwood will execute the deletion semantics chosen by Customer (soft delete or hard delete) and provide a signed deletion receipt containing requestor identity, time of request, deletion mode, and cryptographic hash of the deleted artifact. For Customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments, Redwood will coordinate immediate purge of backups where operationally feasible."

Notes:
- For hosted customers, immediate purge of third-party-managed backups may not be possible; include defined backup-overwrite windows (30/90/180 days) and an exception process for legal holds.
- We should offer an optional BAA / HIPAA addendum for this account and reference SOC 2 Type II (we have a mechanism to provide report under NDA).

- Residency: confirmed, must be us-east-1 only.
- Backups: 90-day overwrite window acceptable for hosted, but we will request Dedicated if we need guaranteed immediate backup purge.
- Redaction: we will adopt client-side tokenization for SSNs and policy_number with a mapping vault we control; ingest-time hashing is acceptable for less-sensitive fields (phone/email).
- Deletion: we require a deletion receipt for all deletion requests; if we move to Dedicated, we will require backup purge coordination language in the contract.
